tweaks.name: Meta OS updates
tweaks.summary: Keeps the headset on its rooted firmware: the OTA switch is off and the updater app is disabled. An OS update could replace the rooted boot image.
tweaks.author: PrivateQuest setup + Bubbagum88
tweaks.check: echo "ota=$(getprop persist.ovr.ota.enabled)"; if pm list packages -d | grep -qx package:com.oculus.updater; then echo updater=disabled; else echo updater=enabled; fi

controls.label: Block OS updates
controls.on: setprop persist.ovr.ota.enabled false; pm disable-user --user 0 com.oculus.updater
controls.hint: OTA switch off and com.oculus.updater disabled
controls.confirmOff: This lets Meta install OS updates again. An update can replace the rooted boot image and undo these fixes. Allow OS updates?

tweaks.name: Meta app auto-updates blocked
tweaks.summary: Fix 08: the OCMS hook stops Meta's apps updating themselves. OCMS itself must stay enabled.
tweaks.author: Bubbagum88
tweaks.check: if sh /data/adb/modules/zygisk_vector/cli scope ls org.codeberg.anonymous950.questenhancer | grep -q com.oculus.ocms; then echo "in scope"; else echo "not in scope"; fi; if pm list packages -d | grep -qx package:com.oculus.ocms; then echo "OCMS DISABLED"; else echo "OCMS enabled"; fi

controls.label: Block Meta app auto-updates
controls.on: sh /data/adb/modules/zygisk_vector/cli scope set org.codeberg.anonymous950.questenhancer com.oculus.systemux/0 com.oculus.vrshell/0 com.oculus.panelapp.settings/0 com.oculus.horizon/0 com.oculus.vrcast/0 com.oculus.ocms/0
controls.off: sh /data/adb/modules/zygisk_vector/cli scope set org.codeberg.anonymous950.questenhancer com.oculus.systemux/0 com.oculus.vrshell/0 com.oculus.panelapp.settings/0 com.oculus.horizon/0 com.oculus.vrcast/0
controls.hint: QuestEnhancer's OCMS hook. OCMS itself must stay enabled.
controls.confirmOff: Meta's apps can update themselves again. That once broke Chats on this firmware. Allow app auto-updates?

tweaks.install: pairing_ctl isn't on this firmware, so pairing from here isn't available.

controls.label: Right controller
controls.hint: Starts a 15 s pairing window: put the controller in pairing mode first

controls.label: Left controller
controls.hint: Starts a 15 s pairing window: put the controller in pairing mode first

tweaks.name: Hand tracking v56 (WIP)
tweaks.summary: Bluedragon's port of the Quest 2 v56 hand tracking engine and models to the Quest 1 DSP: three Magisk modules that must be installed together. Very WIP: about 20 Hz in Steam Link and barely different from stock so far. Not shipped here (Discord attachments, no licence; the engine is Meta's Quest 2 code).
tweaks.author: Bluedragon (Monterey Club)
tweaks.check: n=0; for m in q1_ht56_engine q1_hollywood_dpe q1_hollywood_detection; do if [ -d /data/adb/modules/$m ] && [ ! -f /data/adb/modules/$m/remove ]; then n=$((n+1)); echo "$m installed"; fi; done; [ $n = 0 ] && exit 3; [ $n -lt 3 ] && echo "WARNING: only $n of 3 installed; without all three tracking breaks"; echo "persist.q1.ht56=$(getprop persist.q1.ht56)"
tweaks.install: Not installed. From Bluedragon's Monterey Club Discord post: install q1_ht56_engine, q1_hollywood_dpe and q1_hollywood_detection (all three) in Magisk, then restart.

controls.label: Remove all three
controls.run: for m in q1_ht56_engine q1_hollywood_dpe q1_hollywood_detection; do [ -d /data/adb/modules/$m ] && touch /data/adb/modules/$m/remove; done; resetprop -p --delete persist.q1.ht56; echo "Removed at the next restart"
controls.confirm: Remove Bluedragon's three hand tracking modules and their setting? Stock hand tracking comes back after a restart.

tweaks.name: Wired Steam Link
tweaks.summary: Fix 13: Steam Link streams over the USB cable, with Wi-Fi as a backup. The headset gets 10.86.13.37 on the cable and gives the PC 10.86.13.38. Needs the patched Steam Link app from misteranderson91's patcher, made from your own SteamVR copy.
tweaks.author: misteranderson91
tweaks.check: m=/data/adb/modules/q1_steamlink_usb; [ -d $m ] || exit 3; if [ -f $m/disable ]; then echo module=off; else echo module=on; fi; if ip -4 addr show usb0 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'inet 10.86.13.37/'; then echo cable=up; else echo cable=down; fi
tweaks.install: Not installed: flash 13-wired-steamlink-rN.zip in Magisk, then restart. You also need Steam Link patched for the Quest 1.

controls.label: Cable link
controls.run: if ip -4 addr show usb0 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'inet 10.86.13.37/'; then echo 'Cable link up: headset 10.86.13.37'; else echo 'No cable link (plug in the USB cable)'; fi; tail -n 3 /data/adb/q1_steamlink_usb.log 2>/dev/null

controls.label: Steam Link
controls.run: pm path com.valvesoftware.steamlinkvr >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo 'Steam Link not installed: patch it with the patcher first'; exit 0; }; monkey -p com.valvesoftware.steamlinkvr -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1 >/dev/null 2>&1; echo 'Opening Steam Link'

tweaks.name: Wireless adb on port 5555
tweaks.summary: Fix 01: adb over Wi-Fi on a fixed port with no pairing, after every restart. Anyone on the same Wi-Fi can connect while it's on: use it on a trusted network.
tweaks.author: Bubbagum88

controls.label: Fixed port 5555
controls.hint: Takes effect at the next restart
controls.confirmOff: After the next restart adb works over USB only, until you set this again. Turn it off?

tweaks.name: Chats crash loop
tweaks.summary: Fix 02: Chats (com.oculus.socialplatform) needs a class this firmware doesn't have and crashes every few seconds. Disabling it stops that. Don't uninstall it: that makes Presence crash instead.
tweaks.author: Bubbagum88
tweaks.check: if pm list packages -d | grep -qx package:com.oculus.socialplatform; then echo chats=disabled; else echo chats=enabled; fi

controls.label: Chats disabled
controls.confirmOff: Chats will crash every few seconds again. Enable it?

tweaks.name: Android Developer options
tweaks.summary: Fix 03: Android's Developer options page crashed on open (SELinux kept it from reading memory info). The module allows exactly those reads.
tweaks.author: Bubbagum88
tweaks.check: m=/data/adb/modules/quest1_devsettings_fix; [ -d $m ] || exit 3; if [ -f $m/disable ]; then echo module=off; else echo module=on; fi
tweaks.install: Not installed: flash 03-devsettings-selinux-rN.zip in Magisk, then restart.

tweaks.name: Boot logo
tweaks.summary: Fix 05: your own logo, picked at random each boot, in the boot animation instead of the Meta logo. The first ~2 s Meta logo is in signed firmware and can't change.
tweaks.author: Bubbagum88
tweaks.check: m=/data/adb/modules/quest1_boot_logo; [ -d $m ] || exit 3; if [ -f $m/disable ]; then echo module=off; else echo module=on; fi; echo "logos=$(ls /data/adb/modules/quest1_boot_logo/logos 2>/dev/null | grep -c '\.png$')"
tweaks.install: Not installed: put your logos in fixes/05-boot-logo/module/logos and flash the zip in Magisk.

controls.label: Pick another logo for the next boot

tweaks.name: Charging sound
tweaks.summary: Fix 11: plays your own sound when you plug the headset in (or replaces any other UI sound with qesound). Put a real .ogg file at /sdcard/QuestEnhancer/sounds/charging.ogg. Changes play after a restart.
tweaks.author: Bubbagum88, after a Monterey Club Discord tip
tweaks.install: Not installed: flash 11-charging-sound-rN.zip in Magisk, then restart.

tweaks.name: Display brightness
tweaks.summary: Fix 12: holds the display backlight at a value you choose while the display is on (never while it's off). A brighter panel runs warmer and an OLED ages faster; the system's own value is the safe choice.
tweaks.author: Bubbagum88, after a Monterey Club Discord tip
tweaks.check: if [ -d /data/adb/modules/quest1_backlight ]; then qebacklight status; else echo "now=$(cat /sys/class/leds/lcd-backlight/brightness)"; echo "max=$(cat /sys/class/leds/lcd-backlight/max_brightness)"; echo pin=missing; fi

tweaks.name: Display panel and 90 Hz
tweaks.summary: Which display panel this headset has. Juspertinry's 90 Hz mod needs a boot image retimed for your panel: its dtpatch.py defaults to Samsung (--panel sdc); AUO panels need --panel auo. 90 Hz itself is a boot flash, so it's linked, not switched here.
tweaks.author: Juspertinry
tweaks.check: pt=$(getprop ro.boot.panel_type); d=$(grep -o "mdss_dsi_[a-z0-9_]*" /proc/cmdline | head -1); case "$d" in *auo*) p="AUO: build the 90 Hz boot image with --panel auo";; *sdc*) p="Samsung: the 90 Hz default boot image fits";; *) p="driver not found in the kernel command line";; esac; echo "Panel: $p"; echo "panel_type ${pt:-not set}, driver ${d:-unknown}"
